title: An interrupted setup resumes from its journal and never deletes valid content
statement: Killing setup after its journal has begun leaves a journal naming the last completed phase and an exact resume command; running that command completes the remaining phases. Killing it during the dependency bootstrap, which runs before any journal exists, leaves consumer project state unchanged, and rerunning setup repeats the locked install safely. A failure in any agent phase leaves an already-initialised planning scaffold in place and reports partial setup rather than rolling it back.
notes: PASS 2026-09-23 on EVD-0138, measured by killing real children rather than by making one throw. Inside the bootstrap, which runs before any journal exists: the project is byte-identical afterwards, no `.pi` survives, and an ordinary rerun completes. After the journal opens: what the killed run left records the phase in flight as running — true only because that status is written before the work — and carries an exact resume command naming the project. THE ARGUMENTS ARE PARSED OUT OF THAT COMMAND, not typed beside it, so a command naming another project, omitting `--resume`, or missing altogether fails the control; running them completes the remaining phases and leaves no journal. A failure in an agent phase leaves the scaffold and reports partial setup. THE MEASUREMENT FOUND FOUR DEFECTS IN THE LOCK, EACH FOUND BY THE CONTROL WRITTEN FOR THE ONE BEFORE IT, ALL NOW FIXED, AND ALL THE SAME MISTAKE: judging a file and then removing it, when what was judged can be replaced in between. A killed run's lockfile made every rerun wait out the two-minute stale window; clearing such a lock by read-then-unlink lets two recoveries both acquire; claiming it by rename moves a lock that went live in the meantime, leaving the name free for a waiter, which four racing recoveries caught in CI; and reclaiming the gate introduced for that had the same shape again. Removing somebody else's lock is now serialised behind a gate beside it, taken by the recovery path and the waiter's stale break alike, with the judgement made inside it; reclaiming an abandoned gate is serialised by a token; and the token is never reclaimed, so a leaked one fails closed — the command refuses with exit code 17 and names both files to remove. Setup still refuses another machine's lock, an unreadable one, and a live one.
